```plato

    //==
    // # The mass-spring solver
    //
    // The same graph read as forces instead of constraints: every distance
    // constraint becomes a damped Hookean spring, the forces are summed per
    // vertex, and the result is integrated with the same Verlet step
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft-body_dynamics).
    //
    // It is here because it fails instructively. Explicit integration of a
    // spring is stable only while the step is shorter than the spring's own
    // period, so raising `Stiffness` past what `TimeStep / SubStepCount`
    // supports makes the cloth oscillate and then diverge — visibly, in one or
    // two seconds. The position-based solver above never does that at any
    // stiffness, and putting the two side by side over the same graph is the
    // clearest statement of why position-based dynamics exists.
    //
    // The force sum is a GATHER: for each vertex, fold over every spring and
    // take the ones that touch it. That is O(vertices * springs) per substep,
    // the same as the Gauss-Seidel sweep, but with one array rebuilt per
    // substep instead of one per constraint. A scatter would be cheaper and is
    // exactly what purity does not offer without a per-vertex adjacency table.

    // The force one spring exerts on the vertex numbered `index`: Hooke's law
    // along the spring axis plus a damper on the closing speed. Zero when the
    // vertex is not an end of this spring, which is what lets the whole set be
    // summed by a fold with no adjacency structure.
    SpringForceOn(vertices: Array<ClothVertex>, c: ClothDistanceConstraint, index: Integer, settings: MassSpringSettings, dt: Duration)
        : Vector3D
    {
        var isEnd = c.VertexA.Value == index || c.VertexB.Value == index;
        var near = c.VertexA.Value == index ? c.VertexA : c.VertexB;
        var far = c.VertexA.Value == index ? c.VertexB : c.VertexA;
        var offset = vertices[near.Value].Position - vertices[far.Value].Position;
        var axis = offset.NormalizeOr(Vector3D.Zero);
        var stretch = offset.Magnitude - c.RestLength.Meters;
        var closing = (vertices[near.Value].Velocity(dt) - vertices[far.Value].Velocity(dt)).Dot(axis);
        var magnitude = settings.Stiffness.NewtonsPerMeter * stretch
                      + settings.Damping.NewtonSecondsPerMeter * closing;
        return isEnd ? axis * magnitude.Negative : Vector3D.Zero;
    }

    // The acceleration every spring together imparts to one vertex: the summed
    // force divided by the vertex's mass, i.e. multiplied by its inverse mass,
    // so a fixed vertex feels nothing.
    SpringAccelerationOn(vertices: Array<ClothVertex>, constraints: Array<ClothDistanceConstraint>, index: Integer, settings: MassSpringSettings, dt: Duration)
        : Vector3D
        => constraints.Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (total, c) => total + SpringForceOn(vertices, c, index, settings, dt))
            * vertices[index].SolverInverseMass;

    // One explicit substep: external accelerations plus spring accelerations,
    // integrated with the same Verlet step the position-based solver uses.
    // Bend constraints are ignored — this solver has no force form for them.
    SubStepMassSpring(self: Cloth3D, forces: ParticleForces3D, settings: MassSpringSettings, time: Number, dt: Duration): Cloth3D
        => self.WithVertices(self.Vertices.Count.MapRange(i =>
            self.Vertices[i].Integrate(
                forces.AccelerationAt(self.Vertices[i].Position, self.Vertices[i].Velocity(dt), time)
                    + SpringAccelerationOn(self.Vertices, self.DistanceConstraints, i, settings, dt),
                dt,
                settings.VelocityDamping)));

    // One whole explicit step, divided into `SubStepCount` substeps. Substeps
    // are the only lever this solver has against divergence, short of lowering
    // the stiffness.
    StepMassSpring(self: Cloth3D, forces: ParticleForces3D, settings: MassSpringSettings, time: Number): Cloth3D
    {
        var seconds = SafeDivide(settings.TimeStep.Seconds, settings.SubStepCount.ToNumber, settings.TimeStep.Seconds);
        return settings.SubStepCount.MapRange(i => i)
            .Reduce(self, (current, i) =>
                current.SubStepMassSpring(forces, settings, time + i.ToNumber * seconds, new Duration(seconds)));
    }

    // One whole explicit step of a mesh-bound cloth.
    StepMassSpring(self: ClothMesh3D, forces: ParticleForces3D, settings: MassSpringSettings, time: Number): ClothMesh3D
        => ClothMesh3D(self.Cloth.StepMassSpring(forces, settings, time), self.Faces);

    //==
    // # Reading the result back
    //
    // The simulated positions rebuilt into the geometry the rest of the library
    // already renders. The face tables never moved, so this is a position
    // substitution and nothing more: normals, bounds, triangulation and every
    // other mesh path work on the result with no new plumbing.

    // Every vertex position, in vertex order.
    Positions(self: Cloth3D): Array<Point3D>
        => self.Vertices.Map(v => v.Position);

    // The cloth's triangles as an indexed mesh, sharing the cloth's vertex
    // numbering.
    ToTriangleMesh(self: Cloth3D): TriangleMesh3D
        => (self.Positions, self.Faces);

    // The source polygon mesh with the simulated positions substituted in: the
    // original topology, quads and all, at its current shape.
    ToPolygonMesh(self: ClothMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => (self.Cloth.Positions, self.Faces);

    // The cloth's triangles as an indexed mesh.
    ToTriangleMesh(self: ClothMesh3D): TriangleMesh3D
        => self.Cloth.ToTriangleMesh;

    //==
    // Pinning, which is the other thing a caller needs between build and step.

    // The cloth with one vertex pinned or released.
    WithPinnedVertex(self: Cloth3D, index: VertexIndex, pinned: Boolean): Cloth3D
        => self.WithVertices(self.Vertices.WithVertex(index, self.Vertices[index.Value].WithPinned(pinned)));

    // The mesh-bound cloth with one vertex pinned or released.
    WithPinnedVertex(self: ClothMesh3D, index: VertexIndex, pinned: Boolean): ClothMesh3D
        => ClothMesh3D(self.Cloth.WithPinnedVertex(index, pinned), self.Faces);

    // Every vertex of one grid row pinned: the rail a hanging curtain hangs
    // from. Precondition: the cloth was built from this grid.
    WithPinnedGridRow(self: ClothMesh3D, grid: ClothGrid3D, row: Integer): ClothMesh3D
        => grid.ColumnCount.MapRange(column => grid.GridVertexIndex(column, row))
            .Reduce(self, (current, v) => current.WithPinnedVertex(v, true));
}
```
